articles.title: Vuelta a España: giant hail forces stage three abandonment in Pyrenees
articles.summary: Huge hailstones prompt organisers to act 15km from end. Riders seen heading into hotel on route to take cover. A torrential hailstorm in ⁠the French Pyrenees forced the ⁠abandonment of ⁠the ​third stage of the Vuelta a ⁠España on Monday.
body: The third stage of the Vuelta a España ended without a winner after being halted because of hail on Monday.

Riders started taking shelter in shops and restaurants by the road with about 15km to go on the difficult 174km route from ‌Gruissan to ‌Font-Romeu that was due to finish in the French Pyrenees. Organisers neutralised the race as the peloton scaled the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began pelting the ‌riders, with ice on the road and the threat of lightning. They eventually suspended the stage and declared no winner.
“For the security of the riders, stage three has been cancelled due to hail and severe weather,” race organisers said. “There will be no winner and no podium ceremony.”

The riders started communicating and asking each other to slow down when the hail began. Mats Wenzel of Equipo Kern Pharm and Lorenzo Fortunato of XDS Astana were in a breakaway at the time the race was called off.

articles.title: Liverpool are still haunted by the mess of last summer | Jonathan Wilson
articles.summary: Sunday’s draw with Newcastle shows Andoni Iraola’s new ideas as manager will need to overcome the squad’s lack of balance. Sign up for our free newsletter here. The good news for Liverpool is that, Arsenal aside, every other team with vague title aspirations who played over the weekend looked…
body: The main theme of the first three days of the new season was the value of stability. Manchester City under a new manager were poor and fortunate to overcome Bournemouth. Aston Villa, after big changes of players and backroom staff, were hammered at Brighton. Tottenham, midway through yet another overhaul, were dismal in losing at Brentford. Manchester United at least provided a degree of stability by looking very much like the United of the past decade in their defeat to Hull.

Liverpool, for much of the first 96 minutes of their fixture at St James’ Park, looked like joining the list of challengers struggling to emerge from a summer of churn. Arne Slot spent much of last season complaining about how opponents always scored with their first chance and about Liverpool’s inability to deal with direct attacks, and as Anthony Elanga put Newcastle ahead, it seemed that not much had changed. Joe Willock’s goal to restore the Newcastle lead was much the same: opponents running at pace through vacant space.

articles.title: Julián Alvarez walks alone at Atlético in transfer saga with no end – and no winners | Sid Lowe
articles.summary: Barcelona target left exposed after draw with Villarreal as supporters vented their fury at his ‘dream’ to leave. Julián Alvarez entered a long, dark tunnel on his own. “We’re stronger together,” Giuliano Simeone said but that wasn’t the way it went.
body: Alvarez walked alone. Head down in silence, as he had been all afternoon and beyond, he set off slowly across the pitch accompanied only by his thoughts and the whistles that followed him. Not offered a hand to shake or a nod of acknowledgment, he stepped past the Atlético badge on the touchline where the mouth of the tunnel opens. Either side, supporters hung over the void, whistling and shouting. Way off to his left, Atlético’s other players paused, seemingly waiting for him to slip out of sight before approaching the stand, but none turned back. A scarf was thrown, landing at Alvarez’s feet and left lying there. And then he disappeared into the dark, a portrait of the place he is in.

Good? “Unhappily, this situation isn’t comfortable for anyone,” Jan Oblak said, and amid the damage done, the mutual accusations, the hurt pride and spited faces, nor is it easy to see a solution. The situation, in short, is this: Julián Alvarez wants to leave for Barcelona. Barcelona want to sign him. But he has a contract until June 2030, a €500m buyout clause, and Atlético won’t sell him. And definitely not to them. And so, here they are. Stuck.

articles.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says it is "particularly pleasing" to name seven uncapped players who impressed in the Women's Interprovincial Championship in his squad for the WXV Global Series.
body: Forwards Jemima Adams Verling, Sophie Barrett, Beth Buttimer and Kate Jordan will all be hoping for a Test debut next month, as will backs Caitriona Finn, Lucia Linn and Alana McInerney.
Ireland will play USA and Japan at home in September, before a pair of October Tests against South Africa in the new format of WXV.
In between, they will also play a second game against Japan that does not form part of the series.
Munster trio Buttimer, Finn and McInerney were involved in the wider Six Nations squad this year, as were Connacht's Adams Verling and Ulster prop Barrett.

articles.title: Does Elliott have a Liverpool future after latest omission?
articles.summary: Harvey Elliott's position at Liverpool looks uncertain following his absence from the matchday squad at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.
body: It was a little under a month ago when in the bowels of the Yankee Stadium in New York, Harvey Elliott spoke candidly about his emotions after a "tough" loan spell at Aston Villa and why this summer felt like a second chance for Liverpool.

There was a smile on his face when he spoke about his love for the club - the team he has supported since he was a boy - and wanting to be free and enjoying himself again with his football, because he felt like he had not done that enough.
You only had to see Elliott's joy when he came off the bench in Liverpool 's friendly against Monaco earlier this month as all four sides of Anfield stood up and applauded to see what it meant.

With a number of senior first-team players absent, Elliott started Liverpool 's first friendly under Andoni Iraola in Nashville and again when Liverpool took on Wrexham in New York four days later but as the World Cup contingent returned, the midfielder was benched and where he stood in the squad became clearer.

articles.title: England drop Carse after nightclub incident
articles.summary: Pace bowler Brydon Carse is removed from England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan following an incident that led to him being handcuffed by police.
body: Images that appeared on social media on Sunday showed Carse, 31, in handcuffs outside a bar in Derby on Saturday night.
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has referred the incident to the Cricket Regulator.
The Regulator will investigate and, as a result, Carse has been removed from the squad and replaced by Sonny Baker.
It is the latest in a string of off-field incidents involving the England team - Carse has become the third player this summer to miss a Test because of a disciplinary issue.

articles.summary: Sheffield United boss Chris Wilder has confirmed the club are interested in signing free agent Adam Webster. The defender left Brighton after suffering an ACL injury but Wilder has backed the 31-year-old to make an impact in the near future should the deal be completed.
body: “I’ve known Adam for a long time and he’s coming off the back of a big injury but not a career ending injury, an ACL, at Brighton and out of contract,” Wilder said.

Webster would not be ready to play immediately if he joins, with Wilder confirming the former Brighton defender still needs to complete a medical and build up his fitness after missing pre-season.

articles.title: Middlesbrough land ninth summer signing
articles.summary: Middlesbrough have completed the signing of former Leeds United defender Sam Byram, their ninth acquisition of the summer. The 32-year-old rejected a contract renewal at Elland Road and has signed for Boro as a free agent.
body: The full-back arrives at the Riverside with plenty of experience. He has played more than 200 Championship matches, as well as 60 in the Premier League. Byram is also the first of Boro’s summer recruits that is older than 24.
“I’m buzzing to be here,” Byram said after signing. “It’s a club I know well from playing against them over many seasons, so I’m very familiar with the place and delighted to be here.

“It’s a great club and a big club, and one that I’m really happy to be part of. I’ve been around this league for a number of years and had a couple of promotions in that time, so I know what it takes.
“It’s an incredibly tough league and a long season, but it’s a great squad and great group. If I can add a bit of experience and a bit of quality, that’s what I’m here to do.”

articles.title: Is Norris now Antonelli's biggest title threat?
articles.summary: While he won neither of the race formats across the Zandvoort Sprint weekend, Kimi Antonelli increased his overall world championship lead at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break.
body: The Mercedes driver now leads both team-mate George Russell and Ferrari rival Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, the second-largest advantage Antonelli has enjoyed at the top of the Drivers' Championship so far this season.

But Antonelli's advantage over the driver now occupying fourth place in the standings was cut by a further eight points, following reigning champion Lando Norris' second successive Grand Prix victory, which moved him to within 83 points of the championship lead.

Norris became just the second driver after Antonelli to claim consecutive wins this season, with the McLaren driver's Zandvoort triumph coming after he overtook the championship leader on track. Antonelli had initially reclaimed the lead from Norris at the restart following the red flag triggered by Max Verstappen's heavy lap-one crash.
Yet does the result mean that Norris' hopes of retaining his world title, which seemed all-but over just a few races ago before McLaren brought a notable car upgrade to Budapest, are firmly back on?

articles.title: Saints skipper Hastings gets three-game ban for punch
articles.summary: St Helens captain Jackson Hastings' season could be over after being handed a three-match ban for violent conduct following his sending off in their win over Castleford Tigers on Saturday.
body: Hastings was dismissed in the first half of the 36-12 victory after punching Castleford's Tyler Dupree, who was sin-binned for the same incident.

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports: "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face."
The win keeps Saints' play-off hopes alive, though they are currently on 28 points and seventh in the standings, one place outside of the play-off positions with three games to go.

It means that should they fail to leapfrog one of Hull KR (sixth, 30 points), Leigh Leopards (fifth, 32 points) or Wakefield Trinity (fourth, 32 points) down the stretch, Hastings will have played his last match of the season.
